description: LDL-C fall when 1% of energy from SFA is replaced by carbohydrate (so SFA in place of carbohydrate raises LDL-C by this much)
source: Mensink RP. Effects of saturated fatty acids on serum lipids and lipoproteins. WHO 2016 (as on the 2026 cards and deck slide 17)
notes: Mixed SFA. 0.033 mmol/L x 38.67. The same coefficient is used in card math and the full model. 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C fall when 1% of energy from SFA is replaced by cis-MUFA
notes: Implies MUFA in place of carbohydrate = 1.3 - 1.6 = -0.3 mg/dL per 1% energy (full model only) 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C fall when 1% of energy from SFA is replaced by cis-PUFA
notes: Implies PUFA in place of carbohydrate = 1.3 - 2.1 = -0.8 mg/dL per 1% energy (full model only) 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C rise when lauric (12:0) + myristic (14:0) acid replace carbohydrate
source: Mensink 2016 (WHO) individual fatty acids: lauric about 0.052 and myristic about 0.048 mmol/L per 1% energy
notes: Used only when the SFA split is switched on. Check the individual-fatty-acid table before release. 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C rise when palmitic acid (16:0) replaces carbohydrate
source: Mensink 2016 (WHO) individual fatty acids: about 0.039 mmol/L per 1% energy
notes: Used only when the SFA split is switched on 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C rise when stearic acid (18:0) replaces carbohydrate
source: Mensink 2016 (WHO) individual fatty acids: about 0.004 mmol/L per 1% energy (not significant)
notes: Used only when the SFA split is switched on. Other SFA (short and medium chain; 20:0+) use beta_sfa_cho. 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.

description: LDL-C rise when trans fat replaces carbohydrate
source: Mensink RP et al. Am J Clin Nutr 2003;77:1146 (about 0.040 mmol/L per 1% energy)
notes: Full model only 95% interval is approximate (check against the source); used for coefficient uncertainty.
